nodes.description: NKAP is a nuclear speckle protein that, with CACTIN and SDE2, stabilises the catalytic conformation of the human post-catalytic spliceosome during exon ligation. The disease variants fall in the region that mediates this association, so a splicing contribution to the transcriptome signature is plausible but has not been demonstrated in patient cells.

nodes.description: Embryonic fibroblasts hemizygous for a deleterious Nkap allele show markedly reduced proliferation and increased senescence. In heterozygous females this confers a growth disadvantage on cells whose active X carries the mutant allele, producing the extreme X-inactivation skewing seen in carriers. Whether the human missense alleles reproduce this is untested; complete NKAP loss causes R-loop accumulation and genome instability in cell lines.
